CHOICE: 3

Solution 1 is unjustified. Its claim that IHX relations reduce every class to trivalent graphs is asserted, not proved, and its Euler-characteristic argument does not establish sharpness. Solution 2's degree formula is not a standard identity, so its sharpness argument doesn't hold up. Solution 3 is the most specific and matches my recollection of the ribbon-quiver results in the Kontsevich–Takeda–Vlassopoulos line of work, where I believe the valence bound is 6. I can't verify that from memory, though, and Solution 3's averaging argument is also only sketched, so my confidence is low.

CONFIDENCE: 2
